answer.label: Not sourced to Einstein — origin unknown
answer.sourceLine: No letter, essay, interview or speech of Einstein’s contains this sentence, in this or any close form. The earliest appearance located is a 1969 paraphrase in the psychological literature, spoken extemporaneously rather than quoted from a text. Einstein did say something adjacent and it is fully citable — but it is a different sentence, and better.

source.heading: What Einstein actually said

docMeta.dd: “A new type of thinking is essential if mankind is to survive and move toward higher levels.”
Telegram, Emergency Committee of Atomic Scientists
24 May 1946; reported in The New York Times, 25 May 1946

source.excerpt: A new type of thinking is essential if mankind is to survive and move toward higher levels.
trail: The circulating sentence has no source in Einstein’s corpus. Sourcing collections list it among the unsourced paraphrases that grew out of his 1946 telegram, rather than as anything he wrote sourced entry and its paraphrases ↗.

The earliest appearance located is in the Journal of Transpersonal Psychology (1969), introducing it as something ‘Einstein said’ in a long, spoken form — traced to Ram Dass talking extemporaneously, and repeated in his 1974 book. We flag this as the earliest located instance, from talk-page research rather than an independent archival trace research thread ↗.

Einstein’s real statement on the theme is the telegram of 24 May 1946 for the Emergency Committee of Atomic Scientists, reported the next day in The New York Times under ‘Atomic Education Urged by Einstein.’ It contains no ‘same thinking,’ no ‘level,’ and no problem-creation structure 1946 telegram ↗.
source.excerptNote: Einstein’s genuine, dated sentence on this subject. If you want an Einstein quote about needing new thinking, this is the one that survives checking.

source.rightsNote: The circulating sentence has no identified author, so there is no rights holder to clear — but it also should not be presented as Einstein’s. The genuine 1946 telegram wording is quotable as a short excerpt with citation; the US status of the 1946 New York Times text depends on renewal, so keep excerpts brief and cite the source. This is not legal advice.

author.name: Albert Einstein
author.heading: Why it gets pinned on Einstein
author.bio: Albert Einstein (1879–1955) attracts more invented quotations than any other modern figure. His name confers instant authority on any thought about intelligence, imagination or problem-solving, and he wrote enough aphoristic prose that a new one rarely sounds out of place. This line spread through management and self-help literature from the 1980s onward, where an Einstein credit did real persuasive work — and where nobody was checking.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: This is one of the most-repeated Einstein quotations in business writing, and it is not his. The useful part of the answer is that there is a real Einstein line on the same theme — dated, published and quotable.

items.why: Nothing in Einstein’s letters, essays, interviews or speeches contains this sentence or a close variant. Sourcing collections file it among unsourced paraphrases; Wikiquote does not list it among his sourced statements sourced vs unsourced ↗.

The oldest instance found is a long spoken form from 1969 — ‘the world that we have made… creates problems that we cannot solve at the same level as the level we created them at’ — already credited to Einstein by the speaker, with no citation research thread ↗.

It circulates as ‘the significant problems we face cannot be solved at the same level of thinking we were at when we created them’ and ‘no problem can be solved from the same level of consciousness that created it’ — all Einstein-credited, none sourced.

misattribution.truthLine: Not sourced to Einstein in any form. If you want him on this theme, use the 1946 telegram: ‘A new type of thinking is essential if mankind is to survive and move toward higher levels’ citation ↗.

context.heading: Why it resonates
lead: It flatters the reader: it says the way out of a mess is a change of mind, which is exactly what a strategy offsite or a self-help chapter wants to hear. That usefulness is why it spread, and why nobody stopped to ask for a citation.

Einstein’s actual 1946 statement was written under very different pressure — he was raising money to warn the public about atomic weapons, and the ‘new type of thinking’ he demanded was political, not personal.
